title: Apache HugeGraph Server — Gremlin Sandbox Bypass RCE (CVE-2024-27348)
vuln_pattern: HugeGraph Server (1.0.0–1.3.0) exposes the Gremlin API unauthenticated at POST /gremlin; its sandbox is a SecurityManager that only enforces on threads NAMED 'gremlin-server-exec'/'task-worker', so renaming the current thread via reflection disarms it and reflection-built ProcessBuilder gives RCE.
exploit_steps: Fingerprint HugeGraph (graph-DB branding, the Gremlin console; affected 1.0.0 – 1.3.0). The Gremlin API is POST /gremlin (NOT under /apis/).

The sandbox is a custom SecurityManager that only blocks dangerous calls when the current thread's NAME starts with 'gremlin-server-exec' or 'task-worker'. Bypass: use reflection to RENAME the current thread to anything else — Class.forName("java.lang.Thread").getDeclaredField("name").setAccessible(true), then field.set(Thread.currentThread(), "x").
Construct java.lang.ProcessBuilder itself via reflection (getConstructor(List.class) + newInstance + getMethod("start").invoke) and start the command (e.g. sh -c 'cat /flag').
Read the process output in the same script via commons-io IOUtils.toString(process.getInputStream()) and return it in the Gremlin response.
source: original: CVE-2024-27348 public advisory (Gremlin sandbox bypass)
preconditions: HTTP access to the HugeGraph Gremlin endpoint
verify_oracle: ProcessBuilder command output with the flag
pitfalls: a plain `new ProcessBuilder(...)` is blocked — the check is thread-NAME-based, so renaming the current thread via reflection must come FIRST; do NOT grep the whole filesystem for local templates
post the script to /gremlin with "language": "gremlin-groovy" — /apis/* is the REST API surface, not the Gremlin endpoint
build ProcessBuilder through reflection too; after the rename the constructor itself is what trips the check if invoked directly
